texts.facts: 2. Brief facts of the case are that on 01.10.2018, on receipt of DD no.41A regarding MLC no.500127518/18 from AIIMS Trauma Center, HC Omprakash reached AIIMS hospital. Statement of victim Naveen was recorded wherein he stated that on 01.10.2018 he was traveling from East of Kailash towards Okhla via Nehru Place on his motorcycle bearing no.DL-3SCN-6780. At about 2:30-02:40 pm, when he reached just before u-turn at Kalka Mata flyover, an ECO Sport car bearing no.CH-41T-4762 (hereinafter referred to as the offending vehicle), came at a very high speed and hit the motorcycle of the victim from behind. Due to the impact, victim fell on the road and sustained injury on the left side of his hand and leg. The driver of the offending vehicle took the injured to Spring Meadows Hospital, East of Kailash from where injured was referred to AIIMS Trauma Center. Driver of the offending vehicle then took the injured to AIIMS Hospital and left. A chargesheet was filed before concerned criminal court against driver of the offending vehicle while the present DAR was filed before this Tribunal. 4. As per record, Respondent no.1 is the driver, respondent no.2 is the owner of the offending vehicle and respondent no.3 is insurance company with which the offending vehicle was insured. 5. Respondent no.1 and 2 filed their reply denying the involvement of the offending vehicle or rash and negligence on the part of respondent no.1. It has further been pleaded that the vehicle was duly insured with respondent no.3. In order to prove his claim, petitioner/injured examined himself as PW-1. To prove his claim, petitioner /Naveen Tiwari led evidence by way of affidavit as Ex.PW1/A. He deposed on the lines of the DAR. He stated that on 01.10.2018 at around 02:30 to 02:40 pm, when he ws going to Okhla from his home via Nehru Place by his motorcyle bearing no.DL34CN6780 and when reached at Kalka Mata flyover, just before U-turn, the offending vehicle bearing no.CH41T-4762 brown color coming from behind in a rash and negligent manner and hit the him from back side. Due to the impact, PW-1 fell on the road and sustained grievous injuries on his left side hand and leg. PW-1 further deposed that he moved to Spring Hospital East of Kailash, new Delhi where he was took first aid then shifted to JPNA Trauma Center, New Delhi. During medical treatment, he was transferred to Safdarjung Hospital on the same day where he was discharged. He again admitted in Max Hospital for 3 days where PW1 was operated his leg. 10. In the present case, petitioner has testified as PW-1 to allege that factum and manner of accident. Further, after investigation, even the police had filed chargesheet against respondent no.1 u/s 379/338 of IPC which is also suggestive of negligence of respondent no.1 in causing the accident. Accordingly, issue no.1 is decided in favour of petitioner and against the respondents. The petitioner has not claimed any disability on account of injuries suffered by him. As already discussed, principal award amount/ compensation will be payable by insurance company with simple interest @7.5% p.a. from the date of filing of DAR till actual realization. Insurance company is hereby directed to deposit the award amount in favour of the petitioner with State Bank of India, District Court Complex, Saket Court Branch, New Delhi by way of RTGS/NEFT/IMPS in account of MACT PARKING FUND, A/c No. 00000042706875094, IFS Code SBIN0014244 and MICR code 110002342 under intimation to the Nazir along with calculation of interest and to the Counsel for the petitioner. Respondent side shall also furnish TDS certificate, if any to the petitioner.
texts.arguments: Reliance is placed upon decision in Bimla Devi & ors. vs. Himachal Road Transport Corporation & Ors. (2009) 13 SC 535, in Parmeshwari vs. Amir Chand & Ors., 2011 (1) SCR 1096 and National Insurance Company Ltd. vs. Pushpa Rana, 2009 ACJ 287, wherein it has been held that the negligence has to be decided on the touchstone of preponderance of probabilities and a holistic view has to be taken. In National Insurance Co. vs. Pushpa Rana 2009 ACJ 287 Delhi, it was laid down that completion of investigation and filing of chargesheet are sufficient proof of negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle. 12. Further, respondents have pleaded contributory negligence on the part of the petitioner by alleging that the accident took place due to disbalancing of the motorcycle on which petitioner was travelling. It has been alleged that the motorcycle got disbalanced as the petitioner was carrying load beyond permissible limit and thus, deduction on the account of contributory negligence be made. 13.
